key_insight: Interpretable multi-gene expression programs can predict which lupus nephritis patients respond to specific treatments, with strong performance for MMF and AZA but weak performance for HC and standard of care.
clinical_relevance: These response signatures could support pre-enrollment patient selection for trial enrichment and help avoid enrolling patients unlikely to benefit from a given therapy.
method: Reconstructed a lupus nephritis gene-expression cohort (GSE224705; 21,914 genes; 319 samples) across four regimens.
Built compact, interpretable multi-gene programs separately for MMF, AZA, HC, and standard of care.
Compared program performance and pathway enrichment across treatments, and tested stability versus differential-expression lists.
evidence_signal: Patient-level validation showed AUROC 0.847 for MMF and 0.866 for AZA, versus 0.718 for HC and 0.623 for standard of care, with SOC near chance (MCC 0.119; balanced accuracy 0.555).
watch_item: These findings are based on retrospective transcriptomic data from one cohort, so external validation and prospective testing are needed before clinical or trial-design use.
paper_title: Interpretable biomarker programs predict treatment response in lupus nephritis: patient-level validation across four regimens
